subject.title: feat(android): durable offline command outbox for chat sends

question: Should Android text-only offline commands persist private command text in the shared destructively migrated chat cache database, and what migration, retention, deletion, and diagnostics-redaction guarantees are required before merge?
rationale: The PR intentionally turns user-authored commands into durable on-device state and keeps destructive Room migration semantics, which is a privacy and upgrade boundary automation should not choose for maintainers.

options.title: Require durable outbox guarantees first
options.body: Keep the PR open and require non-destructive or explicitly accepted storage ownership, fixed delivery semantics, and real Android proof before merge.

options.title: Accept staged storage risk
options.body: Maintainers may explicitly accept app-private text storage and destructive schema-bump loss for this staged Android feature, but that acceptance should be recorded before landing.

options.title: Narrow the feature scope
options.body: Reduce the PR to a nonpersistent or foreground-only queue until maintainers approve persistent private command storage.

recommendation.title: Require durable outbox guarantees first
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open and require non-destructive or explicitly accepted storage ownership, fixed delivery semantics, and real Android proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: @steipete has the strongest current history on the stacked Android chat/cache/outbox branch and the relevant Android chat/gateway code.
